answer.rationale:
The pressing symptoms are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so simplify_onboarding plausibly addresses both with one slot. I am deliberately not chasing the competitor with promotional_pricing: memory_73 is the one memory that retained full downstream detail, and it shows the pattern that matters here — headline acquisition gains (+31% new accts, +18% booked rev) purchased with a 12pp drop in first-term renewals among exactly the price-sensitive segment the competitor is targeting. Against a 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective that is a negative-value trade, and the competitive pressure makes it more tempting, not more correct. Referral incentives (memory_57) target established customers and do not touch the declining funnel metrics; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is credible but addresses a different segment than the SMB erosion and would leave both declines unattended.

I am spending verification on memory_86 and memory_31 rather than on memory_73 precisely because memory_73 already carries its own counter-evidence, while the two memories underwriting my intended action are compressed summaries stated only in upstream terms ('completion rates', 'first-week activation') with no renewal, retention, or qualified-pipeline figures. That is the same shape memory_73 would have had if consolidation had dropped its renewal line. Two specific things I need from the archive: (1) whether memory_86 and memory_31 are genuinely independent experiments or one experiment consolidated twice, since two mutually-reinforcing summaries create false confidence; (2) whether the original records tracked anything downstream of activation, or whether the 'durable lift' claim in memory_31 was only ever measured at week one.

The concrete downstream risk: cutting required signup fields can raise activation while degrading lead qualification and self-serve fit, converting a completion-rate win into lower-quality accounts and weaker qualified revenue — an effect invisible in the metrics these memories report. So this runs as a standard experiment with renewal-cohort and qualified-pipeline guardrails read alongside completion rate, not a broad rollout. If verification shows the two memories are one source, or that no downstream metric was ever collected, I will drop to a small guarded test or shift to activation_messaging (memory_91), which is in-product and does not touch qualification gating.
